newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-WHITE SOX SIGN BELLE TO RICHEST-EVER DEAL.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-WHITE SOX SIGN BELLE TO RICHEST-EVER DEAL.

text.p: Free-agent slugger and baseball bad boy Albert Belle Tuesday signed the richest contract ever for a player in his sport, as the Chicago White Sox agreed to pay him a reported $10 million a season.
The five-year contract for the Cleveland Indians outfielder will put Belle in a murderous lineup right behind White Sox home-run theat and 1995 Most Valuable Player Frank Thomas.
The club did not disclose the size of Belle's deal, reported by the Chicago Sun-Times and Chicago Tribune to be worth $50 million or more.

Belle, third in American League MVP voting last year, led the league with 48 home runs and 124 runs batted with a .311 batting average. In the past five seasons, Belle's 234 home runs and 711 runs batted led the major leagues.
"He likes the idea of hitting behind Frank Thomas and being in Chicago," White Sox owner Jerry Reinsdorf said at a news conference held at the team's offices in Comiskey Park.

Belle has had several scrapes with the league and was suspended last season for a violent collision with a second baseman. Before that, he was suspended for hitting with a corked bat, and has engaged in numerous tirades at reporters.
"I'm looking forward to moving on, and to putting all that behind me," Belle said.
Belle's contract, added to Thomas' $7 million salary and multi-million dollar deals for other White Sox players, will lift one of baseball's highest payrolls to more than $50 million a season.

"It's going to make him the highest paid player in baseball, but that's not important," Reinsdorf said. "We're really going for it this year," he added, insisting he would not shed expensive players to make room for Belle.
